title: The Eternal Priest and the Spiritual Priests
english: Nor is it endured to what extent he is left behind. And to say collectively, all those approaching the Savior turn about in the midst of those standing always and continuously in holiness to partake of him. One of those turning about in this way sang to the King of all: 'Against angels I will sing to you.' (Zach. III, 8-9: 'Hear, then, O Jesus, the great priest, you and those near you and those sitting before your face, because they are men of wonders. Because behold, I am bringing my servant to the east, because upon the stone which I gave before the face of Jesus, upon the one stone, seven eyes are.')

The angel testifying to Jesus, the great priest, says these things: 'Hear, you, Jesus, being the great priest; and let those near you and those sitting before your face hear also, being men of wonders, because I call my servant to the east, because upon the stone which I gave before the face of Jesus, seven eyes are upon it.'

The great priest Jesus, who was previously given according to the order of the priesthood of Melchizedek, concerning whom the Apostle writes to the Hebrews: 'Therefore, holy brothers, partakers of a heavenly calling, understand the apostle and high priest of our confession, Jesus, being faithful to him who made him' (Heb. 3:1).

And see that those able to understand how faithful he is to him who made him, the apostle and high priest of our confession, are found to be holy, partaking of a heavenly calling. For it is not for everyone to see how faithful he is to him who made him, the apostle and priest Jesus, but only for him who is able to speak in all things with wisdom to the perfect, he who is able to say: 'I have seen Jesus' with the eyes of my heart enlightened toward the true light.

Therefore, those not partaking of the heavenly calling are negligent, and from this word they themselves are deceived, having been previously misled, saying that the Son of God is a creature and a work. But the foolish stumble thoughtlessly, taking 'him who made him' to mean creation and production into being, the writer of the epistle not intending this. For to become the faithful apostle and high priest is made manifest as certain and immovable to be apostle and priest; for one is not always apostle and priest.

He is Jesus, but from the time when those to whom he is sent and for whom he intercedes exist, through whom the descent here has happened of the one sent by the Father, when 'bending heaven he descended' (Ps 18:4) to those to whom he was sent and of whom he is priest.

Many scriptures signify the certain and unshakeable through the faithful. For that which is said about God: 'All his commandments are faithful, established for an age of ages' (Ps 89:35), and that: 'I will give you the faithful blessings of David' (2 Sam 7:12), and even that: 'I will raise for myself a faithful priest' (Ps 110:4), declare the certain and unchangeable, of the commandments of God existing faithful according to the spiritual law because of the unchangeable, and of the commandments according to the shadow of the law being transferred from the letter to the spirit and from the shadow to the truth.

By this theory also [are] those of the true David, in whom the Savior is according to man, whose faithful blessings are to remain forever, the words of him remaining even if heaven and earth pass away; therefore also a faithful priest exists, having an unshakeable priesthood for the age, becoming and having been shown according to the order of Melchizedek. To this great priest the angel of the Lord says: 'Hear then, O Jesus, the great priest, you and those near you' (Zech 6:5), the spiritual priests, those having been appointed under you being high priest, to whom also in Isaiah it is said they are righteous ones: 'But you shall be called priests, servants of God' (Isa 61:6). And they possess this promise especially, those who through all-pervading holiness in celibacy serve God.

Not only, however, do these hear of the angel with Jesus the great priest, but also those sitting before his face. These are those in the regeneration according to the resurrection of the dead sitting before the face of the Savior, being judge and king, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

These who hear the divine words of the angel with Jesus are not others than the apostles; being near him and sitting before his face, they are not found to be infants or children, but perfect men having encountered the perfect man of the fullness of the knowledge of the Son of God. Therefore also they are observers of wonders, wisely attending to the wondrous powers of...

title: The Sign and Wonder of Christ's Incarnation
english: Of the Lord, as to how to grasp what is made manifest through them. Of this knowledge, the great hierophant Moses and his brother Aaron the high priest are [examples]; for it has been written, 'God set among them the words of His signs and His wonders' (Ps 105:7). How then is the divinely-inspired observer not merely looking at the sight of wonders and signs, but at their words, according to which these things are accomplished?

And it is to be testified by the theory of one and two [things] recorded in the Gospels: a sign and a wonder was the leading of the blind man from birth to sight (Matt 9:27-31), his eyes having been anointed with clay, having been brought from the ground and from the spittle of the benefactor. Because of this having happened paradoxically, the one observing the prototype made manifest through it is a wonder-observer.

For the people from the nations, who previously were not seeing at all, should be considered to be blind from birth by the subversion of atheism and ignorance of God, having looked up then when, having known Christ according to the flesh, the eyes were anointed with the clay made from the spittle of Jesus, having gained experience of the incarnation which brought him to see Him. Alongside these is also the woman with the flow of blood for all twelve years (Luke 8:43-48), who had become outside the bearing of unclean blood through which she was prevented from giving birth, from touching the hem of Jesus. Paradoxically and wondrously it was accomplished; the one having gained knowledge of it is a wonder-observer, transferring that which happened wondrously to the woman into the purified Church from the nations.

Having shown all things observed in the existing words, 'I, says the Almighty Lord, lead my servant toward the East,' calling Him his servant, He who happens to be of the seed of David according to the flesh, 'the one having taken the form of a servant, having emptied himself while being in the form of God' (Phil 2:7). This servant of God who was brought low is that East concerning which it is said in the Gospel: 'An East from on high, to shine upon those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death' (Mal 4:2), no other being 'of the true light.' Showing His own servant, the Father says: 'Behold, a man, East is his name' (Mal 4:2), calling him a man because of the incarnation, and East because of having been raised up, being a sun of righteousness; for indeed it has been written about him in the last of the Twelve Prophets, from the person of the one who sent...

title: The Fig and the Vine
english: "The stone which was rejected by you, the builders, has become the head of the corner." [Ps 118:22]. For how did the two walls not join and complete one single corner: the one being built from the Jews coming to the gospel, and the other from the Gentiles who believed? For when the Church of both Jews and Greeks was gathered, Christ having become its head, He completed one corner, with all those joined to one building in one faith, all people from the two peoples being created into one new man [Eph 2:15].

This stone, thus announced as the cornerstone, chosen, precious, which God placed in the foundations of Zion, no longer to be shamed by any sin, having become pure for everyone believing upon it. Those coming to the immortal living Word, living themselves, are being built up as hidden stones, so that a spiritual house may be composed and an intelligible altar, upon which the sacrifice of praise is offered and all things being like it are spiritual.

May we also, living, become holy stones, rolling upon the earth of God, so that, having been built up on the foundation of the apostles and prophets of Christ Jesus [Eph 2:20], we may be completed as a temple and a spiritual house, so that God may dwell in us.

"I dig a pit," says the Lord of all, "and I will search out all the injustice of that land in one day" [Zech 3:9]. "On that day," says the Lord of all, "let each call his neighbor under the vine and under the fig tree" [Zech 3:10].

"I dig," says the Lord of all, "a pit, in order to make all the hidden things manifest, in order to touch and feel all the injustice of that land;" it is clear that of the one being dug, in the one day of illumination, then most especially when "the Lord God shines" [Ps 104:4] the Lord of all "the secrets of darkness, and makes manifest the purposes of the hearts," in order to condemn those having done all injustice.
One day can be called the season of our Savior's visitation, in which the benefactor who shines also searches all the injustice of the revealed land, taking away the sin of the world.

Because of this, once the cause of all strife and every unjust war has been overcome, there will be a deep peace, such that no one fears anymore, since strifes are dissolved and wars are ended, and the demons and other opposing powers, which are called 'rulers of this darkness', are gone, so that everyone may live fearlessly and invite his neighbor under the fig and the vine.

This peaceful and stable state is being described, and the prophet Micah foretells presciently that day, saying: 'Each one will call his neighbor and his brother under his fig tree and his vine, not being afraid' (Micah 4:4). For how can anyone still be afraid, when all strifes and wars are dissolved?

What is meant by the mentioned plants, the vine and the fig trees—whether the contemplative or the active life? The vine, producing fruit that makes the contemplative and scientific life joyful, and the fig, being somewhat severe and rough due to the toil and sweat for the sake of possessing virtue.

Regarding the fig thus given, the proverb says: 'He who plants a fig tree will eat its fruits, but he who guards the Lord will be honored' (Proverbs 12:14), which is not contrary to history; for many having planted a sensible fig tree neither sat down nor ate its fruits, either being prevented by death or being driven far away from the plant they planted, while only he who eats the fruits of a spiritual tree eats alone and for all.

The fig is said to be the active and energetic life of good things; likewise the vine should be understood, becoming like a branch of the true vine. For each of the disciples of Jesus is a vine, becoming a branch of the one saying, Savior: 'I am the vine, you are the branches. Every branch remaining in me bears more fruit' (John 15:5).
